description: Every IERS-issued end-of-day UTC leap-second is rejected with weekday_mismatch because _check_weekday validates the post-rollover date against the pre-rollover weekday name. Verified live against 7 real historical leap-seconds: 1994-06-30, 1995-12-31, 2005-12-31, 2008-12-31, 2012-06-30, 2015-06-30, 2016-12-31 — all raise InvalidFormat(weekday_mismatch). Mid-day :60 (e.g. 08:49:60) parses correctly, confirming the bug is specifically the ordering of rollover-then-weekday-check. Fix: check weekday of the pre-rollover date in _parse_imf/_parse_rfc850 before _build_datetime rolls the leap-second (or skip the weekday check when _build_datetime returned a _LeapSecondDatetime).

description: Unicode whitespace (NBSP U+00A0, EM SPACE U+2003, IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE U+3000) is silently accepted in place of RFC 9110 SP. Verified live across all 5 documented positions (after comma, in date, leading, trailing, in weekday) and across all 3 dialects (imf/rfc850/asctime). text.split() with no sep argument splits on any Unicode whitespace run, and _strip_trailing_ws only knows ASCII whitespace. RFC 9110 §5.1.1 grammar defines SP as %x20 (single ASCII space). Interop gap vs httpdate which DOES reject non-ASCII whitespace.

description: _LeapSecondDatetime inherits from datetime; .second reads as the post-rollover 0, not the literal 60. Callers checking dt.second == 60 will never see the leap-second flag. README documents is_leap_second() as the right API, but the class doesn't expose a .second==60 shortcut, and __repr__ hides the semantic. Fix is documentation only (or override .second — at risk of breaking datetime invariants).
source: T01 manual audit; live-verified at HEAD 14295be
stack:
# No exception — parser returns _LeapSecondDatetime with .second=0
# instead of .second=60. is_leap_second() is the only introspection.
python -c "from htdate_pure import parse, is_leap_second; dt=parse('Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:60 GMT'); print(dt.second, is_leap_second(dt))"
# -> 0 True
